newsitem.title: UK: Rank makes disposals, sees charges.
newsitem.headline: Rank makes disposals, sees charges.

text.p: British leisure firm Rank Group Plc said on Thursday it had made disposals of peripheral businesses totalling over 200 million stg since the half year and added that it expected to take restructuring charges.
The company also said it sold coach holiday operator Shearings to a new firm formed by NatWest Ventures Ltd and Shearings' management team for 83 million stg.
Rank said it would use the proceeds to cut debt.
The company said its provision for its previously-announced restructuring plans in 1996 would be about 35 million stg, most of which would be spent next year.
Rank also said it decided to revert to historical cost for the carrying values of properties on its balance sheet.
At the year end, the company's property revaluation reserve, which stood at 186 million stg at year-end 1995, will be reversed, Rank said.
The reversal will result in a charge of about 150 million stg for permanent diminution, the company said.
Of that amount, about two-thirds was related to Rank's bingo and UK holiday operations.
Rank said both the restructuring cost and the permanent diminution would be charged to operating profit at the year end.
For the purpose of calculating headline earnings, the permanent diminution will be excluded, the firm said.
Rank said it expected non-operating items to include a net loss on disposals of about 50 million stg, mainly historic goodwill previously written-off to reserves.
The company said it expected investment expenditure for the year to December 31 to total some 900 million stg compared with 366 million stg last year.
This year's total will include capital spending of about 485 million stg and acquisitions of 415 million stg, the firm said.
Regarding Rank Xerox, the firm's venture with Xerox Corp, the company said a payment of 40 million stg net would be received before year-end 1996, compared with 53 million stg net for 1995.
The company, reiterating that it does not plan to keep its interest in Rank Xerox in the long-term, said part of the reduction was due to its reduced stake in the venture.
Rank's shares were marked down 9.5p at 432.5 by 0820 GMT.
Besides Shearings, Rank said it sold Kingston Plantation for about 30 million stg, its inland amusement arcade business for 25 million stg, and Precision Industries for 72 million stg.
At November 30, the company had net debt of about 1.0 billion stg, with just over half held in dollars and most of the rest in pounds.
